unit.title: Data
unit.blurb: Reading and drawing bar charts, dot plots, waffle diagrams and pie charts, grouped frequency diagrams, line graphs and scatter graphs.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Represent and interpret categorical data in bar charts, dot plots, waffle diagrams and pie charts.

O2.t: Represent and interpret grouped data in frequency diagrams, and data that changes over time in line graphs; read scatter graphs.

sections.title: Bar charts, dot plots, waffle diagrams and pie charts

p: A **bar chart** uses bars to show how many are in each group. Always read the **scale** on the axis carefully.
A **dot plot** shows each value as a dot. A **waffle diagram** is a 10 × 10 grid: each square is **1%**. A **pie chart** shows each group as a slice of a circle.
If the scale goes up in 2s, a bar halfway between 8 and 10 shows 9.

req.prompt: The bar chart shows favourite sports. How many children chose swimming?
The waffle diagram shows the percentage of a class that walk to school. What percentage do NOT walk?
How many children are shown in the bar chart altogether?
The pie chart shows favourite pets. Which pet is the most popular?
Use the bar chart to complete the table.

req.prompt: A dot plot shows the number of pets owned by 12 children: 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6. What is the mode?
How many more chose the most popular sport than the least popular?
Explain how to read a bar whose top is halfway between 10 and 12 on the scale.
req.model: The scale goes up in 2s, so the gap from 10 to 12 is 2. Halfway is 1 more than 10, so the bar shows 11.
req.reason: The scale goes up in 2s, so the gap from 10 to 12 is 2. Halfway is 1 more than 10, so the bar shows 11.

sections.title: Frequency diagrams, line graphs and scatter graphs

p: A **frequency diagram** shows grouped data, such as heights 120–129 cm, 130–139 cm. The bars touch because the groups follow on from each other.
A **line graph** shows how something changes over time, such as temperature through a day.
A **scatter graph** plots pairs of values. If the points go up from left to right, as one value increases the other tends to increase.
Use a ruler to read across from a point to the axis.
